reviewNote: Our current take for agentic coding across the major labs. S splits into Frontier, the most capable models for hard work, and Chores, the best value for routine work. Same-tier order is editorial, not a measured gap. Models reviewed but not shown are listed in notShown with the reason.

models.name: Opus 5.5
points: #1 in Agent Arena, FrontierCode, Rails and Theo’s audit.
Priciest per task: $10.53 a Rails run.
models.rationale: S Frontier and the leader: first in Agent Arena (+20.9% against +14.7% for the next model), AA’s FrontierCode 1.1 (52.2%), Agents on Rails (65.3%) and Theo’s blind architecture audit (8.40). It is not first everywhere: Sonnet 5.5 and Muse Wonder Full score 68 to its 66 on AA’s Coding Agent Index, and it costs the most per Rails run. Kirill’s view that it leads almost every metric holds against this evidence.

leadCheck.note: Still #1 after Muse Wonder Full and Gemini 4 Argon launched.
leadCheck.reason: Muse Wonder Full scores 68 on AA’s Coding Agent Index, above Opus 5.5’s 66, but trails it in Agent Arena (+11.3% vs +20.9%), Code Arena WebDev (1726 vs 1806) and Theo’s audit (7.04 vs 8.40). Google’s Gemini 4 Argon launch chart leads Opus 5.5 on DeepSWE (77.9 vs 74.2), but Argon trails in Agent Arena (+12.0%), Agents on Rails (60.6% vs 65.3%), Epoch’s ECI (165 vs 167) and Theo’s audit (3.95). Neither challenge converges, so the leader holds.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
points: 49% on FrontierCode at $0.81 a task, under a tenth of Opus 5.5’s cost.
Rails’ best value: 60.8% at $0.80 a run.
Behind Opus 5.5 on the hardest work.
models.rationale: S Chores, the clearest value pick: 49.1% on AA’s FrontierCode at $0.81 a task (level with Fable 5.1 at under a tenth of the cost), Rails’ best bang for the buck (60.8% at $0.80), Agent Arena’s cost frontier from $0.22 to $0.65 a task, and 63 on AA’s Coding Agent Index at $1.04 against Sonnet 5.5’s $14.19. Chosen over Sonnet 5.5, which is not cheap per task, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, which AA finds less capable than GPT-6.1 Sol at medium effort for a higher cost per task. Not Frontier: Opus 5.5 leads it in the same tests.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
points: #2 in Agent Arena at +14.7%.
AA: terminal parity with Opus 5.5.
Theo: impressive but inconsistent.
models.rationale: A, first: #2 in Agent Arena and second in Agents on Rails, but behind Opus 5.5 in every reviewed head-to-head and about six times GPT-6.1 Sol’s Rails cost for a similar score. Moved from S when S was limited to the clear best in each lane. It takes the one slot left after each major lab’s best, edging Fable 5.1 in Agent Arena (+14.7% vs +14.2%), Code Arena WebDev and AA’s cost per task. The Rails post replaces OpenAI’s launch thread, which had no scores. Theo’s reliability warning still applies.

models.name: Muse Wonder Full
points: AA coding index: 68, level with Sonnet 5.5.
#7 in Agent Arena, #6 in Code Arena WebDev.
Only in Meta’s Muse Code; no public API.
models.rationale: A: converging independent results from AA (Coding Agent Index 68 in Muse Code, Intelligence Index 56), Agent Arena (#7, +11.3%), Code Arena WebDev (#6, 1726) and Theo’s audit (7.04, level with GPT-6 Astra). Behind Opus 5.5 everywhere except AA’s coding index. Usable only through Muse Code, with no per-token price yet.

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
points: #6 in Agent Arena; 60.6% on Rails, level with GPT-6.1 Sol.
AA: 53, level with GPT-6 Astra; fewest hallucinations.
Theo: 47 of 92 claims false in his audit.
models.rationale: A, last: Agent Arena (#6, +12.0%) and Agents on Rails (60.6% vs GPT-6.1 Sol’s 60.8%) put it with the tier, and AA scores it level with GPT-6 Astra. Held at the bottom of A by Theo’s blind audit (3.95, with half its checked claims false), #10 in Code Arena WebDev and Epoch’s 6th place on software engineering. Its cost per task doubles when the launch discount ends on Nov 30.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
points: #1 open model in Agent Arena, #11 overall.
AA: 45 at $0.26 a task; MIT license.
GPT-6.1 Sol at medium is cheaper and stronger.
models.rationale: B: the strongest open-weights model in both Arena boards (Agent Arena #11 at +5.1% for $0.20 a task) and 45 on AA’s Intelligence Index for $0.26 a task. Not S Chores: AA finds GPT-6.1 Sol at medium effort more capable for less ($0.21, 48), and Arena puts it at about 37% of Sol’s improvement for 27% of the cost. DeepSeek’s own DeepSWE chart is provider-run. FrontierCode and Rails tested the earlier V4.1 Flash, not this build.

models.name: Grok 4.7
points: AA coding index: 56, up from 47 for Grok 4.6.
#18 in Agent Arena; 33.8% on FrontierCode.
Theo reports weak frontend work and loops.
models.rationale: F: shown because it is xAI’s latest model, but cheaper shown models beat it on converging independent evidence. GPT-6.1 Sol leads it in Agent Arena (+13.5% vs +3.2%) and FrontierCode (49.1% vs 33.8%), and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 leads it in Agent Arena (+4.7%) at a fraction of the cost. AA’s matched-effort gains over Grok 4.6 are real but do not close that gap. FrontierCode replaces xAI’s launch chart, which compared mismatched efforts.

notShown.name: Grok 4.6
notShown.note: Rechecked Oct 21: AA’s matched-xhigh Coding Agent Index rises from 47 to 56 with all three components up. Theo’s complaints about 4.7 also call 4.6 slower and less pleasant; no widespread preference for 4.6.

notShown.name: Sonnet 5.5
notShown.note: Opus 5.5 leads it in Agent Arena (+20.9% vs +12.7%), Code Arena WebDev (1806 vs 1769), FrontierCode (52.2% vs 45.8%) and Theo’s audit (8.40 vs 7.88); Sonnet leads only AA’s coding index (68 vs 66) and Terminal-Bench. Not a Chores pick: AA measured the highest cost per coding task of any model, $14.19.

notShown.name: Fable 5.1
notShown.note: Behind Opus 5.5 in Agent Arena (+14.2% vs +20.9%), Code Arena WebDev (1743 vs 1806), FrontierCode (49.0% vs 52.2%) and AA’s coding index (62 vs 66), at a higher AA cost per task ($7.63 vs $5.98). Close to GPT-6 Astra, which took the one spare slot: Astra edges it in Agent Arena and Code Arena WebDev at under half the AA cost per task; Fable edges Astra on FrontierCode (49.0% vs 47.0%).

notShown.name: GPT-6 Luna
notShown.note: Rechecked Oct 21 and kept over GPT-5.6 Luna. Cheapest useful OpenAI model (Agent Arena’s frontier below $0.10 a task), but far behind GPT-6.1 Sol: Agent Arena +3.0% vs +13.5%, Rails 43.5% vs 60.8%, FrontierCode 41.9% vs 49.1%.

notShown.name: Haiku 5.5
notShown.note: 41.8% on FrontierCode and 43 on AA’s Intelligence Index; GPT-6.1 Sol at medium effort scores higher on AA for $0.21 a task. Not a Chores pick.

notShown.name: Muse Wonder
notShown.note: Meta’s API model. Behind Muse Wonder Full in Agent Arena (+3.7% vs +11.3%), Code Arena WebDev (1651 vs 1726) and AA’s coding index (63 vs 68); 46.6% on Rails.

notShown.name: Muse Spark 1.3
notShown.note: AA: Muse Wonder Full improves on it in all ten Intelligence Index evaluations (48 to 56). Agent Arena +3.4%.

notShown.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
notShown.note: The 1017 build gains six points on AA’s Intelligence Index and 52 points in Code Arena WebDev; Agent Arena +2.6% vs +4.7%.

notShown.name: MiMo-V2.6-Pro
notShown.note: AA has it one point above DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (46 at $0.13 a task) and 45.4% on FrontierCode, but it trails in Agent Arena (+3.7% vs +4.7%) and Code Arena WebDev (1626 vs 1664). Mixed against DeepSeek, and well behind GPT-6 Astra for the spare slot; over the seven-model limit.

notShown.name: Kimi K3
notShown.note: Over the seven-model limit. Agent Arena +1.8% (#25), Code Arena WebDev 1655, FrontierCode 43.6%, AA 44: behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 at a higher cost.

notShown.name: Qwen3.8-Max
notShown.note: Code Arena WebDev #12 (1672) and 43.2% on FrontierCode for the 0902 build; no Agent Arena or independent coding-agent result for the current build.

notShown.name: Mistral Large 4
notShown.note: Research preview scoring 38 on AA’s Intelligence Index, level with GPT-6 Luna; no reviewed coding-agent result.
